description: PostgreSQL server internals collected by postgres_exporter 0.20.1 on the six database nodes (3 HQ + 3 DR).

panels.title: Instances Up
panels.description: postgres_exporter was able to connect to PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Scrape Errors
panels.description: The last scrape returned an error — metrics below may be stale.

panels.title: Total Connections
panels.description: Sum of active backends across all selected databases and nodes.

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Shared-buffer hit ratio. Below ~99% on an OLTP workload usually means shared_buffers is too small for the working set.

targets.expr: sum(rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum(rate(pg_stat_database_blks_read{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])), 1) * 100

panels.title: Primary / Replica Role
panels.description: Role as PostgreSQL itself reports it. Compare with the Patroni dashboard — they must agree.

targets.expr: sum by (site, instance) (pg_stat_database_numbackends{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"})

panels.title: Connection Utilization %
panels.description: Against the max_connections setting. Hitting the limit locks everyone out, including Patroni's own health checks.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (pg_stat_database_numbackends{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}) / on(instance) clamp_min(pg_settings_max_connections{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance"}, 1) * 100

panels.title: Rollback Ratio %
panels.description: A rising rollback share points at application errors or serialization/deadlock failures.

targets.expr: rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]) / clamp_min(rate(pg_stat_database_xact_commit{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_database_xact_rollback{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]), 0.001) * 100

panels.title: Rows Read (returned / fetched) per s
panels.description: A large gap between returned and fetched means many rows are scanned to produce few results — missing indexes.

targets.expr: rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]) / clamp_min(rate(pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(pg_stat_database_blks_read{job=~"postgres_exporter_.*", site=~"$site", instance=~"$instance", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]), 1) * 100

panels.title: Block Read / Write Time
panels.description: Requires track_io_timing = on. Zero everywhere means it is off.

panels.title: Temp Files / s
panels.description: Queries spilling to disk because work_mem was too small.

panels.title: Replication Lag (seconds)
panels.description: Time between the last replayed transaction and now, as seen by the replica.

panels.title: Replication Slot Active
panels.description: An inactive slot keeps pinning WAL on the primary — this is the classic way a primary fills its disk.

panels.title: WAL Retained by Slot
panels.description: Bytes of WAL the primary must keep because this slot has not confirmed them yet.

panels.title: Slot Safe WAL Size
panels.description: How much more WAL can be written before this slot is invalidated. Requires max_slot_wal_keep_size to be set.

panels.title: WAL Directory Size
panels.description: A steadily growing pg_wal means archiving is failing or a replication slot is stuck. Cross-check the pgBackRest dashboard.

panels.title: Checkpoints / hour
panels.description: Requested checkpoints dominating timed ones means max_wal_size is too small for the write rate. On PostgreSQL 17+ these live in pg_stat_checkpointer — enable --collector.stat_checkpointer on postgres_exporter.

panels.title: Checkpoint Write / Sync Time
panels.description: Long sync times mean checkpoint fsyncs are stalling on the data disk.

panels.title: Buffers Written / s
panels.description: Who is flushing dirty buffers. On PG 17+ the backend and checkpoint counters moved to pg_stat_io / pg_stat_checkpointer.

panels.title: Buffers Allocated & maxwritten_clean
panels.description: maxwritten_clean counts times the background writer stopped early because it hit bgwriter_lru_maxpages.

panels.title: Restartpoints / hour (replicas, PG 17+)
panels.description: Restartpoints are the replica equivalent of checkpoints. A large gap between requested and done means the replica cannot keep up with the WAL it is replaying — directly relevant to the DR site.

panels.title: Locks by Mode
panels.description: ExclusiveLock / AccessExclusiveLock build-up means blocked queries.

panels.title: Replication Conflicts / s
panels.description: Queries on a replica cancelled because they conflicted with replay. Tune hot_standby_feedback / max_standby_streaming_delay.

panels.title: Dead Tuples (top 10 tables)
panels.description: Bloat waiting for vacuum.

panels.title: Sequential vs Index Scans / s
panels.description: A rising share of sequential scans on a growing table is the earliest sign of a missing index.

options.content:
This dashboard targets **postgres_exporter 0.20.1** against **PostgreSQL 18**.

Most panels use collectors that are **enabled by default**: `database`, `locks`,
`replication`, `replication_slot`, `stat_bgwriter`, `stat_database`,
`stat_user_tables`, `wal`.

Two things need explicit configuration:

| Panel group | Requirement |
|---|---|
| *Checkpoints*, *Restartpoints* | PostgreSQL 17 moved checkpoint counters from `pg_stat_bgwriter` to `pg_stat_checkpointer`. Start the exporter with `--collector.stat_checkpointer`. The `(PG<17)` series are kept as a fallback and stay empty on PG 18. |
| *Block Read / Write Time* | Needs `track_io_timing = on` in the Patroni-managed PostgreSQL parameters. Without it these series are flat zero. |

The exporter connection must also be able to read `pg_stat_*` — grant the
monitoring role `pg_monitor`:

```sql
GRANT pg_monitor TO postgres_exporter;
```

If **every** panel below the overview is empty, check `pg_up` first: when the
exporter cannot connect to PostgreSQL it still exposes its own metrics, so the
target looks healthy in Prometheus while all database metrics are missing.

title: PostgreSQL — HQ & DR
